records.source: וַיְהִ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁמַ֣ע לְסַנְבַלַּ֣ט וְ֠טוֹבִיָּה וּלְגֶ֨שֶׁם הָֽעַרְבִ֜י וּלְיֶ֣תֶר אֹֽיְבֵ֗ינוּ כִּ֤י בָנִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וְלֹא־נ֥וֹתַר בָּ֖הּ פָּ֑רֶץ גַּ֚ם עַד־הָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא דְּלָת֖וֹת לֹא־הֶעֱמַ֥דְתִּי בַשְּׁעָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was when it was heard by Sanballat and Tobiah and by Geshem the Arab and by [the] rest of our enemies that I had built the wall and not was left in it a breach (also until the time the that doors not I had set up in the gates),
pieces: Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that not one gap was left in it, though by then I had not yet hung the doors in the gates.

L.1: And it happened, when it was heard by Sanballat and Tobiah and by Geshem the Arab and by the rest of our enemies that I had built the wall and that no breach was left in it (though up to that time I had not set up the doors in the gates),

R.1: Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab and our other enemies heard that I had finished rebuilding the wall. There were no gaps left in it, though I had not yet put the doors in the gates.

decisions.choice: Geshem the Arab: a ruler of Arab peoples to the south
decisions.reason: Geshem is named with Sanballat and Tobiah as an opponent from the start (2:19). He seems to have led Arab tribes south of Judah, the Arabs of 4:1.

decisions.choice: though the doors were not yet set up: an aside
decisions.reason: Nehemiah adds that the gates still lacked their doors, so the work was not quite finished; this is why he would not leave it (verse 3). The doors were hung later (7:1).

decisions.choice: when it was heard: the sentence goes on into verse 2
decisions.reason: Verse 1 says when the enemies acted; verse 2 says what they did. Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma.

decisions.choice: gap
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "gap" for the breach in the wall, as in 4:1.

records.heading: Come, let us meet together

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח סַנְבַלַּ֤ט וְגֶ֨שֶׁם֙ אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֔ר לְכָ֞ה וְנִֽוָּעֲדָ֥ה יַחְדָּ֛ו בַּכְּפִירִ֖ים בְּבִקְעַ֣ת אוֹנ֑וֹ וְהֵ֨מָּה֙ חֹֽשְׁבִ֔ים לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לִ֖י רָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: and sent Sanballat and Geshem to me, saying, come and let us meet together at Kephirim in [the] plain of Ono; and they [were] planning to do to me harm.
pieces: Sanballat and Geshem sent me a message: "Come, let us meet together at Kephirim in the plain of Ono." But they were planning to harm me.

L.2: that Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, let us meet together at Kephirim in the plain of Ono." But they were planning to do me harm.

R.2: So Sanballat and Geshem sent me a message. "Come and meet with us at Kephirim in the Ono Valley," they said. But they were planning to hurt me.

decisions.choice: Kephirim: a place name, or "one of the villages"
decisions.reason: The word can be the name of a place or the plural of a word for village, "in the villages". The text gives no other village of this name, so either is possible.

decisions.choice: the plain of Ono: far from Jerusalem, near the border
decisions.reason: Ono lay near Lod, in the lowland toward the coast, about a day's journey northwest of Jerusalem (11:35; Ezra 2:33). A meeting there would take Nehemiah away from the work and from his own people.

decisions.choice: they were planning harm: Nehemiah saw through the invitation
decisions.reason: Nehemiah says what he understood, perhaps afterward: the meeting was a trap.

records.source: וָאֶשְׁלְחָ֨ה עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם מַלְאָכִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מְלָאכָ֤ה גְדוֹלָה֙ אֲנִ֣י עֹשֶׂ֔ה וְלֹ֥א אוּכַ֖ל לָרֶ֑דֶת לָ֣מָּה תִשְׁבַּ֤ת הַמְּלָאכָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אַרְפֶּ֔הָ וְיָרַדְתִּ֖י אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I sent to them messengers, saying, a work great I [am] doing, and not I am able to go down; why should cease the work when I let it drop and go down to you?
pieces: So I sent messengers to them with this reply: "I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to come down to you?"

L.3: And I sent messengers to them, saying, "I am doing a great work, and I cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"

R.3: I sent messengers to them with this answer: "I am doing important work, and I cannot leave it to come down to you. The work would stop if I left."

decisions.choice: a great work: a large and important task
decisions.reason: Nehemiah answers without accusing them; the work of the wall is too important to leave.

decisions.choice: go down: from Jerusalem in the hills to the lowland
decisions.reason: Ono was lower than Jerusalem, so a journey there was "going down".

decisions.choice: The work would stop if I left.
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a statement, which says the same thing more plainly.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלְח֥וּ אֵלַ֛י כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אַרְבַּ֣ע פְּעָמִ֑ים וָאָשִׁ֥יב אוֹתָ֖ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And they sent to me according to the word the this four times, and I answered them according to the word the this.
pieces: Four times they sent me the same message, and each time I gave them the same answer.

L.4: And they sent to me in this same way four times, and I answered them in the same way.

R.4: They sent me the same message four times, and each time I gave them the same answer.

decisions.choice: according to this word: in the same way, with the same message
decisions.reason: The phrase means a message of the same kind.

decisions.choice: four times: the enemies kept up the pressure
decisions.reason: The repeated invitation shows how hard they tried to draw Nehemiah away; the fifth attempt (verse 5) changed tactics.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ אֵלַ֨י סַנְבַלַּ֜ט כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֛ה פַּ֥עַם חֲמִישִׁ֖ית אֶֽת־נַעֲר֑וֹ וְאִגֶּ֥רֶת פְּתוּחָ֖ה בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And sent to me Sanballat according to the word the this a time fifth his young man, and a letter open [was] in his hand.
pieces: The fifth time, Sanballat sent his servant to me with the same message, and he had an open letter in his hand.

L.5: And Sanballat sent his young man to me in the same way a fifth time, with an open letter in his hand.

R.5: The fifth time, Sanballat sent his servant to me with an open letter.

decisions.choice: an open letter: unsealed, so others could read it
decisions.reason: Letters were usually sealed. An open letter could be read by the messenger and anyone he met, so the rumor in it would spread whatever Nehemiah answered.

decisions.choice: his young man: his servant or aide
decisions.reason: The word for a young man used for an attendant, as in 4:10.

decisions.choice: Readable leaves out "in the same way"
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out "in the same way", since the letter brings a new message (verses 6-7).

records.source: כָּת֣וּב בָּ֗הּ בַּגּוֹיִ֤ם נִשְׁמָע֙ וְגַשְׁמ֣וּ אֹמֵ֔ר אַתָּ֤ה וְהַיְּהוּדִים֙ חֹשְׁבִ֣ים לִמְר֔וֹד עַל־כֵּ֛ן אַתָּ֥ה בוֹנֶ֖ה הַחוֹמָ֑ה וְאַתָּ֗ה הֹוֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: Written in it: among [the] nations it is heard, and Gashmu [is] saying, you and the Jews [are] planning to rebel; therefore you [are] building the wall, and you [are] becoming their king, according to the words the these.
pieces: In it was written: "It is reported among the nations, and Geshem confirms it, that you and the Jews are planning to revolt. That is why you are building the wall. According to these reports, you are about to become their king.

L.6: In it was written, "It is heard among the nations, and Gashmu says it, that you and the Jews are planning to rebel; that is why you are building the wall. And you are going to become their king, according to these reports.

R.6: The letter said, "People in the nations around here are saying that you and the Jews are planning to rebel against the king. Geshem says so too. They say that is why you are building the wall, and that you plan to make yourself their king.

decisions.choice: Gashmu: another form of the name Geshem
decisions.reason: Gashmu is a longer form of Geshem (verse 1; 2:19), perhaps closer to the way the name was said in Arabic.

decisions.choice: planning to rebel: a charge of treason against the Persian king
decisions.reason: A walled city could resist the king. Judah's enemies had made the same charge to stop the work in the past (Ezra 4:12-16). If the king believed it, Nehemiah would lose his post and perhaps his life.

decisions.choice: according to these words: according to these reports
decisions.reason: "These words" are the rumors the letter repeats.

decisions.choice: Gashmu (Literal); Geshem (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the usual form of the name, so readers see it is the same man as in verse 1.

records.source: וְגַם־נְבִיאִ֡ים הֶעֱמַ֣דְתָּ לִקְרֹא֩ עָלֶ֨יךָ בִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר מֶ֚לֶךְ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְעַתָּה֙ יִשָּׁמַ֣ע לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכָ֔ה וְנִֽוָּעֲצָ֖ה יַחְדָּֽו׃ס
records.gloss: And also prophets you have appointed to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, saying, a king [is] in Judah. And now it will be heard by the king according to the words the these; and now come and let us take counsel together.
pieces: You have even appointed prophets to announce about you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now this report will reach the king. So come, let us talk this over together."

L.7: And you have also appointed prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah!' And now it will be heard by the king according to these words. So now come, and let us take counsel together."

R.7: They also say you have chosen prophets to announce in Jerusalem, 'Judah has a king!' The king of Persia will soon hear about this. So come and talk it over with us."

decisions.choice: prophets to proclaim a king: as prophets once anointed Israel's kings
decisions.reason: In Israel, prophets named and anointed kings (1 Samuel 10:1; 16:13; 1 Kings 1:34). The charge is that Nehemiah was using prophets to back a claim to the throne.

decisions.choice: it will be heard by the king: a veiled threat
decisions.reason: The letter warns that the report will reach Artaxerxes, and offers a meeting as the way to deal with it; it was the same trap as before (verse 2).

decisions.choice: The king of Persia
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the king here is the Persian king, not the king the rumor speaks of.

records.source: וָאֶשְׁלְחָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֤א נִֽהְיָה֙ כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתָּ֣ה אוֹמֵ֑ר כִּ֥י מִֽלִּבְּךָ֖ אַתָּ֥ה בוֹדָֽאם׃
records.gloss: And I sent to him, saying, not it has happened according to the words the these which you [are] saying, for from your heart you [are] inventing them.
pieces: I sent him this reply: "Nothing like what you are saying has happened. You are making it all up in your own mind."

L.8: And I sent to him, saying, "Nothing like these words that you are saying has happened; for you are inventing them out of your own heart."

R.8: I sent him this answer: "None of what you say is true. You are making it all up."

decisions.choice: inventing them: devising them
decisions.reason: The verb means to devise or make up (1 Kings 12:33, of a feast Jeroboam invented). Nehemiah flatly denies the charge.

decisions.choice: from your heart: out of your own mind
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought in Hebrew. The story is Sanballat's own invention.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֻלָּ֗ם מְיָֽרְאִ֤ים אוֹתָ֨נוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִרְפּ֧וּ יְדֵיהֶ֛ם מִן־הַמְּלָאכָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תֵעָשֶׂ֑ה וְעַתָּ֖ה חַזֵּ֥ק אֶת־יָדָֽי׃
records.gloss: For all of them [were] making us afraid, saying, will drop their hands from the work, and not it will be done. And now strengthen my hands.
pieces: They were all trying to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will grow too weak for the work, and it will never be finished." But now, O God, strengthen my hands.

L.9: For all of them were trying to make us afraid, saying, "Their hands will drop from the work, and it will not be done." And now, [O God,] strengthen my hands.

R.9: They were all trying to scare us. They thought, "They will get discouraged and stop working, and the wall will never be finished." But I prayed, "God, make me strong!"

decisions.choice: their hands will drop: they will lose heart
decisions.reason: Hands that drop or go limp are a picture of losing courage (Jeremiah 38:4; Ezra 4:4). The opposite is to strengthen the hands (2:18).

decisions.choice: and now strengthen my hands: a short prayer
decisions.reason: The command has no one named. It is most likely a prayer to God, like Nehemiah's other short prayers (5:19; 6:14). The ancient Greek translation reads "I strengthened my hands", taking it as a statement.

decisions.choice: saying: thinking, as their aim was
decisions.reason: "Saying" here gives the enemies' purpose: what they hoped would happen.

decisions.choice: O God (Balanced); I prayed, "God" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one addressed, to make the prayer clear (m2); Literal brackets it.

records.source: וַאֲנִי־בָ֗אתִי בֵּ֣ית שְֽׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה בֶן־דְּלָיָ֛ה בֶּן־מְהֵֽיטַבְאֵ֖ל וְה֣וּא עָצ֑וּר וַיֹּ֡אמֶר נִוָּעֵד֩ אֶל־בֵּ֨ית הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הַֽהֵיכָ֗ל וְנִסְגְּרָה֙ דַּלְת֣וֹת הַהֵיכָ֔ל כִּ֚י בָּאִ֣ים לְהָרְגֶ֔ךָ וְלַ֖יְלָה בָּאִ֥ים לְהָרְגֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And I went [to the] house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah son of Mehetabel, and he [was] shut in. And he said, let us meet at [the] house of God, inside the temple, and let us shut [the] doors of the temple, for [they are] coming to kill you, and by night [they are] coming to kill you.
pieces: One day I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was confined to his home. He said, "Let us meet in the house of God, inside the temple, and shut the temple doors, because they are coming to kill you. They are coming at night to kill you!"

L.10: And I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was shut in. And he said, "Let us meet at the house of God, inside the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple, for they are coming to kill you; by night they are coming to kill you."

R.10: One day I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel. He was staying shut up in his house. He said, "Let us meet at God's temple, inside the building. Let us close the doors, because men are coming to kill you. They are coming at night to kill you!"

decisions.choice: shut in: confined, for a reason not given
decisions.reason: The word means shut up or kept in. It may mean Shemaiah was confined by ritual uncleanness or illness, or that he shut himself in as a sign to back his warning. The text does not say, and the sense of his being shut in is uncertain.

decisions.choice: inside the temple: the holy place, open only to priests
decisions.reason: The word for temple here is the main hall of the sanctuary, which only priests could enter (Numbers 18:7). Shemaiah proposes that Nehemiah, a layman, hide there.

decisions.choice: they are coming to kill you ... by night: an urgent, repeated warning
decisions.reason: Shemaiah repeats the threat for force, as a prophet's oracle might (verse 12 calls it a prophecy).

decisions.choice: who was shut in (Literal); confined to his home (Balanced); staying shut up in his house (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say where Shemaiah was shut in; Balanced and Readable take it as his own house, where Nehemiah visited him.

records.source: וָאֹמְרָ֗ה הַאִ֤ישׁ כָּמ֨וֹנִי֙ יִבְרָ֔ח וּמִ֥י כָמ֛וֹנִי אֲשֶׁר־יָב֥וֹא אֶל־הַהֵיכָ֖ל וָחָ֑י לֹ֖א אָבֽוֹא׃
records.gloss: And I said, a man like me, will he flee? And who [is] like me who would go into the temple and live? Not I will go in.
pieces: But I said, "Should a man like me run away? And could someone like me go into the temple and live? I will not go in!"

L.11: And I said, "Should a man like me flee? And who [is there] like me who could go into the temple and live? I will not go in."

R.11: But I answered, "Should a leader like me run away and hide? Should someone like me go into the temple to save my life? I will not go!"

decisions.choice: should a man like me flee? A leader must not run
decisions.reason: As governor, Nehemiah's flight would tell the people that the danger was real and would stop the work.

decisions.choice: go into the temple and live: two possible senses
alternatives: go into the temple to save his life
decisions.reason: "And live" may mean "and survive", since a layman who entered the holy place could die for it (Numbers 18:7). Or it may mean "to save his life": should someone like me hide in the temple to stay alive? Both readings lead to the same refusal.

decisions.choice: a leader like me; to save my life
decisions.reason: Readable says why Nehemiah's position matters (m1) and follows the second reading of "and live" (m2), which is easier to follow; the footnote gives the other.

records.source: וָאַכִּ֕ירָה וְהִנֵּ֥ה לֹֽא־אֱלֹהִ֖ים שְׁלָח֑וֹ כִּ֤י הַנְּבוּאָה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלַ֔י וְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה וְסַנְבַלַּ֖ט שְׂכָרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And I recognized, and see, not God had sent him, for the prophecy he had spoken against me, and Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
pieces: Then I realized that God had not sent him. He had spoken this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.

L.12: And I perceived, and look, God had not sent him, but he had spoken the prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.

R.12: Then I understood that God had not sent him. He gave me that message because Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to do it.

decisions.choice: God had not sent him: a false prophecy
decisions.reason: A true prophet was sent by God; one who spoke what God had not sent was false (Jeremiah 14:14; 23:21; 28:15). Nehemiah tested the message and saw that it led him toward sin (verse 13).

decisions.choice: against me: the prophecy was aimed at Nehemiah's harm
decisions.reason: "Spoke against me" can mean "spoke concerning me", but the story shows it was spoken to harm him.

decisions.choice: hired him: paid him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of hiring a worker or a mercenary, and of paying a prophet for a word (Deuteronomy 23:5).

records.source: לְמַ֤עַן שָׂכוּר֙ ה֔וּא לְמַֽעַן־אִירָ֥א וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־כֵּ֖ן וְחָטָ֑אתִי וְהָיָ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם רָ֔ע לְמַ֖עַן יְחָֽרְפֽוּנִי׃פ
records.gloss: For this [reason] [was] he hired: so that I would be afraid and act so and sin, and it would become for them an evil name, so that they could reproach me.
pieces: He had been hired to frighten me into doing this and sinning, so that they could give me a bad name and discredit me.

L.13: For this [purpose] he was hired, that I should be afraid and act so and sin, and it would become a bad name for them [to use], so that they could taunt me.

R.13: They paid him to frighten me, so that I would do wrong by going into the temple. Then they could say bad things about me and make me look shameful.

decisions.choice: act so and sin: breaking God's law by entering the holy place
decisions.reason: For a man who was not a priest to enter the sanctuary was a sin (Numbers 18:7; 2 Chronicles 26:16-21). It would also show fear.

decisions.choice: an evil name for them: a scandal they could use
decisions.reason: "An evil name" is a bad reputation (Deuteronomy 22:14). The enemies hoped to discredit Nehemiah before the people.

decisions.choice: by going into the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sin would have been (m1).

records.source: זָכְרָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י לְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה וּלְסַנְבַלַּ֖ט כְּמַעֲשָׂ֣יו אֵ֑לֶּה וְגַ֨ם לְנוֹעַדְיָ֤ה הַנְּבִיאָה֙ וּלְיֶ֣תֶר הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ מְיָֽרְאִ֥ים אוֹתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat according to his works these, and also Noadiah the prophetess and [the] rest of the prophets who were making me afraid.
pieces: Remember, my God, what Tobiah and Sanballat have done, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who have been trying to frighten me.

L.14: Remember, my God, Tobiah and Sanballat, according to these works of theirs, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the rest of the prophets who were trying to make me afraid.

R.14: My God, remember what Tobiah and Sanballat have done. Remember also Noadiah the prophet and the other prophets who were trying to frighten me.

decisions.choice: remember ... according to their works: a prayer that God judge them
decisions.reason: This is the other side of Nehemiah's prayer in 5:19: he asks God to take note of what his enemies have done and to deal with them justly (13:29). He leaves them to God instead of taking revenge himself.

decisions.choice: his works: the works of each of them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "his works", taking the two men one by one; the works meant are those of both.

decisions.choice: Noadiah the prophetess: a woman prophet who opposed Nehemiah
decisions.reason: She is not mentioned anywhere else. Other women prophets in Israel include Miriam, Deborah and Huldah (Exodus 15:20; Judges 4:4; 2 Kings 22:14).

decisions.choice: the prophet
decisions.reason: Readable says "prophet" for a woman too, the plain modern word.

records.heading: The wall finished in fifty-two days

records.source: וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ הַֽחוֹמָ֔ה בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לֶאֱל֑וּל לַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנַ֖יִם יֽוֹם׃פ
records.gloss: And was completed the wall on [the] twenty and five of Elul, in fifty and two days.
pieces: So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-two days.

L.15: And the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth [day] of Elul, in fifty-two days.

R.15: The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul. The work took fifty-two days.

decisions.choice: Elul: the sixth month, late summer
decisions.reason: Elul is the Babylonian name of the sixth month of the year, in August and September. In the twentieth year of Artaxerxes (2:1) this was about 445 BC.

decisions.choice: fifty-two days: a very short time
decisions.reason: The wall was rebuilt on its old foundations and much stone was at hand, but it was still fast work, done under threat. The next verse gives the reason.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ כָּל־א֣וֹיְבֵ֔ינוּ וַיִּֽרְא֗וּ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר סְבִֽיבֹתֵ֔ינוּ וַיִּפְּל֥וּ מְאֹ֖ד בְּעֵינֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֚י מֵאֵ֣ת אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ נֶעֶשְׂתָ֖ה הַמְּלָאכָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: And it was when heard all our enemies, and were afraid all the nations which [were] around us, and they fell greatly in their eyes, and they knew that from with our God was done the work the this.
pieces: When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations around us were afraid and lost all their confidence, for they knew that this work had been done with the help of our God.

L.16: And it happened, when all our enemies heard [it], that all the nations that were around us were afraid, and they fell greatly in their own eyes; and they knew that this work had been done by our God.

R.16: All our enemies heard about it. All the nations around us were afraid, and they lost their pride. They knew that our God had helped us do this work.

decisions.choice: were afraid
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters can be read "they were afraid" or "they saw"; the vowels in the standard text give "were afraid". Either fits: they heard and saw, or heard and feared.

decisions.choice: they fell greatly in their own eyes: they lost their confidence
decisions.reason: To fall in one's own eyes is to lose self-esteem and confidence. The enemies who had mocked the builders (3:33-35) were now humbled.

decisions.choice: done by our God: even the enemies saw God's hand
decisions.reason: The verse echoes Nehemiah's confidence that "the God of heaven will give us success" (2:20). The completion of the wall is evidence of God's help, which the surrounding nations themselves recognized.

records.source: גַּ֣ם׀בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם מַרְבִּ֞ים חֹרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ אִגְּרֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם הוֹלְכ֖וֹת עַל־טוֹבִיָּ֑ה וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לְטוֹבִיָּ֖ה בָּא֥וֹת אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Also in the days the those [were] multiplying [the] nobles of Judah their letters going to Tobiah, and those of Tobiah [were] coming to them.
pieces: Also in those days the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and letters from Tobiah kept coming to them.

L.17: Also in those days the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah's [letters] were coming to them.

R.17: During this time, the leaders of Judah kept sending letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah kept sending letters back to them.

decisions.choice: the nobles of Judah: leading men in contact with Tobiah
decisions.reason: Some of the leading families were tied to Tobiah by marriage (verse 18), so he had friends inside Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: in those days: during the time the wall was being built
decisions.reason: Nehemiah steps back to describe what had gone on alongside the work.

decisions.choice: the leaders of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "nobles", the book-wide term.

records.source: כִּי־רַבִּ֣ים בִּֽיהוּדָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י שְׁבוּעָה֙ ל֔וֹ כִּי־חָתָ֥ן ה֖וּא לִשְׁכַנְיָ֣ה בֶן־אָרַ֑ח וִֽיהוֹחָנָ֣ן בְּנ֔וֹ לָקַ֕ח אֶת־בַּת־מְשֻׁלָּ֖ם בֶּ֥ן בֶּֽרֶכְיָֽה׃
records.gloss: For many in Judah [were] lords of oath to him, for son-in-law he [was] to Shecaniah son of Arah, and Jehohanan his son had taken [the] daughter of Meshullam son of Berekiah.
pieces: Many in Judah were bound to him by oath, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berekiah.

L.18: For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had taken the daughter of Meshullam son of Berekiah.

R.18: Many people in Judah had sworn to be loyal to him. This was because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah. Also, his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berekiah.

decisions.choice: lords of oath to him: bound to him by sworn agreements
decisions.reason: "Lords of an oath" means those who had entered into a sworn agreement, here alliances made through marriage and perhaps business.

decisions.choice: Meshullam son of Berekiah: one of the builders of the wall
decisions.reason: Meshullam repaired two sections of the wall (3:4, 30). Even a loyal builder was tied to Tobiah by marriage, which shows how far Tobiah's influence reached.

decisions.choice: had taken the daughter: had married her
decisions.reason: To take a woman is to marry her (Genesis 24:67).

records.source: גַּ֣ם טוֹבֹתָ֗יו הָי֤וּ אֹמְרִים֙ לְפָנַ֔י וּדְבָרַ֕י הָי֥וּ מוֹצִיאִ֖ים ל֑וֹ אִגְּר֛וֹת שָׁלַ֥ח טוֹבִיָּ֖ה לְיָֽרְאֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Also his good deeds they were saying before me, and my words they were bringing out to him; letters sent Tobiah to make me afraid.
pieces: They kept telling me about his good deeds, and then they reported to him what I said. And Tobiah kept sending letters to frighten me.

L.19: They also kept speaking of his good deeds before me, and they kept carrying my words out to him. [And] Tobiah sent letters to make me afraid.

R.19: They kept telling me what a good man Tobiah was. Then they went and told him everything I said. And Tobiah kept sending me letters to scare me.

decisions.choice: his good deeds: his kindnesses, or his good intentions
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the good things Tobiah had done, or that his intentions were good. Either way, his friends among the nobles spoke well of him to Nehemiah.

decisions.choice: carrying my words out to him: acting as informers
decisions.reason: The nobles who wrote to Tobiah (verse 17) passed on what Nehemiah said in private.

decisions.choice: Tobiah sent letters to frighten me: the last of the enemies' tactics
decisions.reason: The chapter ends as it ran: Nehemiah's enemies tried again and again to frighten him (verses 9, 13, 14).
